1000152905::la.title: Innovation Lawyer - Corporate
1000152905::la.description: At BCLP, we’ve built our firm on the foundations of thinking differently. Curious, inquisitive and unbound by tradition, we’re building change within our sector and beyond. It starts with our people, which is why we need an Innovation Lawyer – Corporate to join our team. Embedded within the Technology Dept, but aligned to our firm’s Corporate & Finance Transactions (CFT) Department and an integral part of the firm’s wider Taskforce for Legal Evolution in AI Program (LEAP), the role of Innovation Lawyer is to develop and drive forward AI strategy and enablement for transactional lawyers in our firm, with a particular focus on corporate and commercial work. Although this role is not predominantly fee earning, the role will require time recording, and some fee earning work is expected. This will be as an occasional timekeeper, with no set targets. This is an excellent opportunity to take on a cutting-edge role within an innovative and forward-thinking firm, in an area of strategic priority. A chance to become involved in firm-wide projects and work collaboratively with other lawyers and business professionals to deliver AI transformation across the Firm’s global network. Remain current in the practice of law by performing some AI-enabled fee-earning work (As agreed for the role), and by working alongside and engaging directly with fee earners across (a) Corporate Transactions, (b) Technology, Commercial & Data Practice Groups, and (c) Tax, Employee Benefits and Private Client practice groups (together “Corporate PGs”). Responsibilities Key responsibilities of this role are set out below. While the jurisdictional focus of this role is mainly on the US, the successful candidate should have a global mind-set and proactively seek to support transformation efforts in BCLP offices outside the US, wherever possible. Work with practice group leaders and partners across the CFT Department, the Director of Practice Operations for CFT and LEAP Leadership to identify the highest value use cases for using AI across Corporate PGs. Work with the LEAP Taskforce to identify and support pilots of the best AI platforms to support those use cases. Collaborate with existing practice-aligned Innovation Teams to maintain a consistent approach to Innovation activities. Where new AI technologies are implemented and approved by the firm: Standardize and scale successful AI solutions across Corporate PGs in close collaboration with the LEAP Taskforce. Serve as a dedicated resource for lawyers seeking AI support, offering responsive, high-touch assistance with prompt design, refinement, and execution. Assist Corporate PGs in identifying and adopting AI-enabled workflows through proactive outreach and hands-on support developing and executing AI templated prompts that align with the work of the Corporate PGs. In conjunction with Learning & Development and the LEAP Taskforce, ensure use of AI is embedded within associate training programs and identify where AI can be used as part of junior associate training. Prepare and deliver technology presentations and trainings related to creative and practical uses for AI across Corporate PGs, and assist in the development of web content that highlights strategies for leveraging AI throughout matter cycles. Develop a detailed understanding of the firm’s other technologies that support delivery of client work within Corporate PGs, and ensure that these are promoted and used appropriately alongside any new AI-enabled practice technologies.This includes close collaboration and working with the firm’s Knowledge Solutions and Innovation teams. Note – this is one of two new roles being created by the firm in this strategically important area. The other role being recruited is an Innovation Lawyer for Finance PGs. Both roles will be aligned to the CFT Department and will work seamless and optimally together to drive AI Transformation across the Department. 1000152909::dallas.description: Overview Orrick’s Energy & Infrastructure Business Unit is seeking a Mid-Level Associate with 3–5 years of environmental law and permitting experience, with exposure to M&A or project finance transactions and a diverse client base, including developers, financial institutions, private equity firms, government entities, and Fortune 500 companies. We pride ourselves on a collegial, innovative environment that is both professionally and personally rewarding. Our firm offers exceptional training and mentoring opportunities and values an entrepreneurial outlook. We’re looking for candidates who are passionate, collaborative, and ready to make an impact. Responsibilities • Advise clients on matters involving environmental statutes and regulations (e.g., CERCLA, NEPA, Clean Water Act, Clean Air Act, RCRA, Endangered Species Act, National Historic Preservation Act). • Support transactions, project development, regulatory compliance and permitting. • Conduct legal research, draft documents, and manage client interactions, and work with environmental consultants. • Work with federal and state agencies on complex matters. • Contribute to a team-oriented environment while managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced practice. Qualifications • JD with strong academic credentials. • Admitted to the Bar in a U.S. state and compliant with local jurisdictional requirements. • 3–5 years of relevant environmental law experience at a top law firm or government agency. • Demonstrated experience with environmental and permitting aspects of M&A or project finance transactions. • Excellent research, drafting, and communication skills. • Strong commitment to client service and teamwork; proactive and eager to learn. How to Apply: Please apply online at https://www.orrick.com/Careers and include a resume, J.D. transcript, writing sample and cover letter. Search firm recruiters must submit using our Search Firm Portal. Please contact recruiting@orrick.com for agreements and login credentials. If you have any questions, please reach out to Zach Smith, Recruiting Manager, at zsmith@orrick.com. We’ll help you to connect with peers and mentors to ensure you are integrated into our client teams. If you are passionate about innovative work in a dynamic environment, you’re just who we’ve been looking for. Compensation and Benefits The expected salary range for this position is between $260,000 and $365,000. Orrick is committed to providing a comprehensive, competitive, and thoughtful total compensation package to our attorneys and staff, wherever they work. 1000152959::dallas.title: eMerge Senior Attorney - All Offices
1000152959::dallas.description: Troutman Pepper Locke’s eMerge offers clients integrated technology and legal solutions to address complex data-driven challenges in litigation, transactional and compliance matters, and government investigations. Our innovative team of tech-literate attorneys and technologists collaborate to deliver solutions tailored to the unique circumstances of each matter but informed by experience across thousands of other engagements. eMerge is seeking an experienced Senior Attorney with minimum five years of experience to join any of our offices in a privileged lead capacity. This role will be the primary guardian of attorney-client privilege and work product protections throughout the document review process, ensuring that privileged material is never produced and that review activities adhere to eMerge’s established privilege protocols. Candidates should have experience serving as the primary point of contact for privilege-related issues arising during document review, designing and implementing privilege sweeps and screens to identify and protect privilege material, consulting with case teams on privilege questions, issues, and strategy throughout the review lifecycle, ensuring all review workflows follow standard eMerge privilege protocols and procedures, drafting and finalizing privilege logs upon completion of review, and escalating complex privilege determinations to senior eMerge attorneys as appropriate. Strong candidates will have demonstrated technical proficiency along with direct experience overseeing and conducting quality control of AI-assisted privilege reviews, including familiarity with the tools and methodologies that support these workflows. Candidates must be licensed and in good standing in the state that they practice. Candidates should also possess: - In-depth knowledge of eDiscovery laws, regulations, and industry best practices. - Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to explain complex legal and technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders. - Fluency with preservation, filtering, and export capabilities of corporate messaging, collaboration, and productivity solutions, including Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. - Expertise with Relativity is strongly preferred. The salary range for this position is $115,000 - $140,000 dependent on relevant years of experience. For inquiries or additional information on this position, please contact Gillian Sacks. By applying for this position, you agree and understand that Troutman Pepper Locke will process your Personal Information pursuant to the terms of our Worker and Applicant Global Privacy Notice.
